messages:
maria: Hey team — customer acct_9832 reports duplicate charges on invoice inv_2026_03_01 after a batch of requests timed out and then retried. They see the same token line twice (≈1200 tokens). Root request id they gave: abc123. Anyone seen similar in the last 24h?
henry: Can you paste the invoice lines + any ledger entries you have? I can start a reconciliation.
maria: Ledger snippet pasted below: 
```
invoice inv_2026_03_01: line A req=abc123 tokens=1200
ledger: charge acct_9832 req=abc123 status=completed tokens=1200
ledger: charge acct_9832 req=abc123 status=completed tokens=1200
```
maria: Customer used our JS SDK v1.4 and did not set an Idempotency-Key header. SDK default retry config = 3 retries on timeout/5xx.
raj: I pulled gateway logs for req=abc123 — shows initial upstream 504 at t0, client retried, second inbound request had same body but no Idempotency-Key. We forwarded both requests to the runtime.
sara: Runtime processed two separate sessions for that account; total token consumption ~2400 in the window 03:14:02 - 03:14:30. Gateway x-request-id differs between the two inbound requests.
ingest-bot: Alert: duplicate-processing-detected acct_9832 count=2 window=1748123400-1748123500
henry: That explains why billing shows two charges — billing reads final token emissions from the runtime and both executions produced tokens. We'll need to refund or adjust ledger entries and add guardrails.
raj: Short-term mitigation idea: detect identical payloads for same api-key within a short window (5-60s) and mark as replay to avoid forwarding. But that could block legitimate duplicates.
sara: Safer: implement server-side idempotency dedupe using a payload-hash keyed by (api_key + payload_hash). TTL 30-60s. Read-before-forward to avoid double-processing when client didn't provide an idempotency key. Low-latency cache (redis/local) should work. I'll open a PR.
maria: Customer wants a timeline and a refund for the duplicate line. Henry, can you handle the credit + reconciliation?
henry: Will do interim credit for inv_2026_03_01 and create FIN ticket. Also running a token-level reconciliation across the runtime vs billing ledger for last 24h to surface similar cases. Ticket FIN-1245 opened.
maria: Repro steps for infra: simulate client no-idempotency, force upstream 504 then automatic client retry. Example (quick):
```
# attacker/client without idempotency-key
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"AAAA... (large)"}' 
# simulate client retry (same body, no idempotency)
sleep 1
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"AAAA... (large)"}'
```
raj: We should also change SDKs to auto-attach an Idempotency-Key per logical request and document recommended retry behavior (no retries on 4xx, exponential backoff, and attach idempotency).
sara: PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/987 — adds dedupe-cache keyed by (api_key, payload_hash) TTL=60s, metric duplicate_replays_blocked, and tracing for payload-hash. Deploying to staging tonight.
henry: I've issued a one-time credit for inv_2026_03_01 and added a note on the invoice. I'll reconcile and post results here when done.
raj: Also adding a gateway log field idempotency_key_or_hash so we can more easily detect replays during postmortem.
maria: Owners: infra(sara/raj) implement dedupe + metric; billing(henry) refund + reconcile; support(maria) notify customer with timeline. ETA 48h.
sara: Merged to staging at 1748123600, running e2e on replay scenarios.
maria: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll close after customer confirms credit shows on their account. Please paste PR + FIN ticket links when available.
